data.headline: Raise price 5% now to cover soaring input costs
data.why: Global cereal prices have jumped over 22% year-on-year, pushing up batter and oil costs that sit behind the 12% exposed share. The model shows the price increase lifts weekly contribution by the figures above while volume holds because 55% of customers prefer you over the rival even at a higher price.
data.watch_out: If the commodity surge deepens or the pound weakens, the 12% cost exposure could widen and erase the gain; watch for a sustained drop in weekly portions sold below the figures above.
data.recheck_when: Next FAO food-price index release or if rival cuts price below 11.15

what_happened.text: Russia invaded Ukraine, the largest exporter of sunflower oil, and its ports were blockaded.
The World Bank's monthly sunflower oil price reached $2,361 a tonne, up from $1,412 in January.
UK chip shops reported sunflower oil up about 60% in a year; the trade body warned a third of shops could close.
The monthly price was back to $1,496 a tonne as Black Sea exports resumed.

caveats: Frying oil is about an eighth of a portion's cost in the owner's own words. In 2022 chip shops were also hit by fish, flour and energy prices; only the oil is scored here.

Prices in pounds are converted at £1 = $1.36, the January 2022 rate. The series is the world sunflower oil price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/mt); a shop buys refined oil from a wholesaler, which moved later.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.
